reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) supports DCT-induced room-temperature strengthening and phase transitions in a related HfNbTaTiZr alloy, but provides no data on elevated-temperature behavior, the effect of subsequent aging, or microstructural stability at 1123 K. Key premises regarding high-temperature performance and aging stabilization are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: DCT after LMD increases residual stress and lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr-based HEAs, improving strength and ductility at room temperature.
DCT can induce phase transitions (e.g., HCP precipitates) in this alloy system without additional deformation.
The proposed aging treatment at ~900°C will stabilize DCT-induced defects and phases, preventing microcracking and uncontrolled transformations.
The combined DCT + aging treatment will inhibit dislocation glide and softening at elevated temperature (~1123 K).
The predicted ~25% yield strength improvement at 1123 K is achievable based on prior room-temperature results.
